source_meta._title: Incorrect Protochunk#setStatus call on chunk generate

stor.environment: Minecraft Java Edition 1.20, launched as an unmodified mapped/decompiled development runtime under a Java debugger. Use the integrated server in a disposable single-player world. The corrective ChunkStatusMixin shown in the report, the 1.20.1 Release Candidate 1 fix version, and any other mod that changes chunk generation must not be loaded.
preconditions: Install and select exactly Minecraft Java Edition 1.20, which is the sole affected version listed by the report.

Have a Java development/debugging environment whose mapped source for ChunkStatus#generate matches the 1.20 implementation quoted in the report. Source line breakpoints and Java step-over operations must work before starting the game.
Do not install or apply the corrective ChunkStatusMixin included in the report; it changes the target call and prevents reproduction of the reported implementation.

Use a new disposable world so that normal spawn-area generation exercises the chunk-status generation pipeline. The report does not provide a required seed, world preset, game mode, coordinates, or server configuration.
Configure the debugger so it does not automatically resume after reaching the target ChunkStatus#generate completion callback.

Keep the debugger's local-variable/object inspection view available so the Observation Agent can inspect this, the pre-work center ChunkAccess referenced as $$7/$$3x in the quoted source, the result Either referenced as $$2x, and the supplied chunk list $$6 after the trigger.

steps.action: Select an exact Minecraft Java Edition 1.20 mapped development launch configuration. Confirm that it is not 1.20.1 Release Candidate 1 or any later version.
steps.success_cue: The selected runtime identifies itself as Java Edition 1.20, the first and only affected version listed in the report.

steps.action: Disable all mods, mixins, patches, or transformed classes that modify ChunkStatus, chunk generation, or chunk conversion. In particular, ensure that the corrective ChunkStatusMixin printed in the report is not present.
steps.success_cue: The runtime will execute the original 1.20 ChunkStatus#generate implementation quoted in the report.

steps.action: In the debugger, open the mapped ChunkStatus class and locate the generate method by matching the method body against the source excerpt in the report. Locate the thenApply completion callback that runs after generationTask.doWork completes.
steps.success_cue: The debugger displays the completion callback containing the ProtoChunk type check and status assignment from the report.

steps.action: Within that completion callback, locate the status-assignment statement that operates on the ProtoChunk derived from the pre-work center chunk.
steps.success_cue: The exact status-assignment line is selected in the original 1.20 implementation, not in the corrective mixin.

steps.action: Set a source breakpoint on the $$3x.setStatus(this) statement. If the debugger supports conditional breakpoints, condition it on the current ChunkStatus being FULL. A suitable condition for a mapped runtime is this == ChunkStatus.FULL; if that symbol cannot be resolved, use this.toString().equals("full") or manually resume non-FULL hits.
steps.success_cue: An enabled breakpoint is visible on the status-assignment line and is configured to stop on the FULL-status invocation, or the executor is prepared to filter hits manually.

steps.action: Optionally set a second breakpoint on the next executable statement after the status assignment, at the profiler-finish check. This provides a stable pause location after stepping over the trigger.
steps.success_cue: The debugger can pause immediately after the target status assignment while the generate callback's local variables remain in scope.

steps.action: Start Minecraft from the selected development launch configuration in debug mode. Allow startup to continue until the Minecraft main menu is responsive.
steps.success_cue: The Java Edition main menu is displayed and the debugger remains attached to the game process.

steps.action: Create a disposable single-player world using the normal new-world path. Leave the seed, world preset, and game mode at their defaults because the report specifies none. Select Singleplayer, select Create New World, enter any recognizable temporary world name, and select Create New World again.
steps.exact_input: Singleplayer -> Create New World -> World Name: MC-263340 reproduction -> Create New World
steps.success_cue: The integrated server begins preparing the new world and generating its spawn-area chunks.

steps.action: Allow world generation to run until the breakpoint in ChunkStatus#generate is reached. If an unconditional breakpoint stops for a status other than FULL, inspect the current ChunkStatus, resume execution, and repeat until the FULL invocation reaches the $$3x.setStatus(this) line.
steps.success_cue: Execution is paused before $$3x.setStatus(this), the current ChunkStatus is FULL, and the branch-local target $$3x is a ProtoChunk obtained from the center ChunkAccess captured before generationTask.doWork.

steps.action: Confirm that the debugger is paused inside the thenApply callback after generationTask.doWork has completed and that the result Either represented by $$2x is already available in the current stack frame. Do not alter any object fields or evaluate methods with side effects.
steps.success_cue: The callback's pre-work chunk reference and completed result are both available for later inspection, and execution remains paused immediately before the status-assignment call.

steps.action: Use the debugger's Step Over operation exactly once to execute the original 1.20 status-assignment statement without entering ProtoChunk#setStatus.
steps.success_cue: The status-assignment call has just returned, and execution is paused on the following statement in the same ChunkStatus#generate completion callback.

stor.handoff_condition: The original Java Edition 1.20 call $$3x.setStatus(this) has just executed for the FULL ChunkStatus, and the debugger is paused immediately afterward with the callback frame and its pre-work chunk reference, completed result Either, and chunk list still available. Hand control to the Observation Agent before resuming world generation or saving and closing the world.
uncertainties: The report contains no formal player-facing Steps to Reproduce. This plan therefore uses a debugger to execute and expose the exact internal call identified by the report rather than inventing a gameplay symptom.

The report does not specify a launcher, mod loader, mappings distribution, decompiler, IDE, debugger, or build configuration. An existing mapped 1.20 development runtime is therefore required, but the exact tooling cannot be selected from the supplied evidence.

The local names $$2x, $$3x, $$6, $$7, and $$8 come from the decompiled source in the report and may differ in another mapped or decompiled environment. The executor must identify variables by their roles and by matching the quoted method body if those names are unavailable.

The report does not state whether a fresh world, an existing world, or both reliably leave the misidentified chunk in a saved or externally visible state. A fresh world is selected only as the simplest deterministic way to exercise chunk generation.

A comment identifies chunk saving as a manifestation, but the report supplies no deterministic save/unload timing that guarantees a particular affected chunk will be written while misidentified. The plan stops at the incorrect internal call rather than fabricating a save-based procedure.
The report's corrective mixin is evidence about the target implementation but is not itself a reproduction prerequisite; loading it would prevent the original call from being exercised.

source_meta.issue links: Relates:outward:MC-299770:Chunks loaded by ender pearls permanently unload upon player death even when enderPearlsVanishOnDeath is set to false
source_meta._title: Ender pearls stop loading chunks in The End after relog, if there are no players in that dimension

stor.environment: Minecraft Java Edition dedicated server running version 1.21.4 with a matching unmodified 1.21.4 client. Use one operator test account in a fresh or disposable world. Command blocks must be enabled, and the dedicated server must remain running and continue ticking normally while the client is disconnected.
preconditions: Install and launch the Minecraft Java Edition 1.21.4 dedicated server and a matching 1.21.4 client.
Set enable-command-block=true in server.properties before starting the server.
Grant the test account operator permission so it can use /gamemode, /execute, /tp, /fill, /setblock, /forceload, and /item.
Use only one connected player. No other player may enter or remain in The End during the reproduction.
Use a fresh or disposable world with no force-loaded chunks in The End and no unrelated ender pearls there.
Keep the dedicated server process running throughout the disconnect and reconnect sequence. Ensure it will continue ticking for at least 20 seconds with no connected players.
Do not use /tick freeze, pause the server, stop the server, or open the test world in a different version during the procedure.
Use default controls unless rebound. T opens chat, right-click uses an item or opens a command block, and double-tapping Space enables Creative flight.
The procedure intentionally uses a remote End location and an artificial platform so the Ender Dragon and terrain do not interfere with the chamber.

steps.action: Start the dedicated server, open Multiplayer on the matching 1.21.4 client, and join with the operator test account.
steps.exact_input: Multiplayer -> select the 1.21.4 test server -> Join Server
steps.success_cue: The test account has finished joining and can move normally in the Overworld.

steps.action: Verify that the test account is the only connected player. Press T, enter the command including the leading slash, and press Enter.
steps.success_cue: The command reports exactly one connected player: the test account.

steps.action: Put the test account in Creative mode for safe construction. Press T, enter the command including the leading slash, and press Enter.
steps.success_cue: The game confirms Creative mode, and the player has the Creative inventory and no Survival health or hunger HUD.

steps.action: Enable Creative flight by double-tapping the jump control, whose default key is Space.
steps.success_cue: The player remains suspended when not standing on a block and can move vertically with Space and Left Shift.

steps.action: Move to a high Overworld location where a safe logout platform can be prepared. Press T, enter the command including the leading slash, and press Enter.
steps.success_cue: The player is flying near X=0.5, Y=305, Z=0.5 in the Overworld.

steps.action: Create a 5-by-5 stone platform below the player. Press T, enter the command including the leading slash, and press Enter.
steps.success_cue: A stone platform covering X=-2 through 2 and Z=-2 through 2 is visible at Y=299.

steps.action: Stand on the center of the prepared Overworld platform. Press T, enter the command including the leading slash, and press Enter.
steps.success_cue: The player is standing safely on the stone platform at approximately X=0.5, Y=300, Z=0.5.

steps.action: Enter Spectator mode so the player can be moved safely to an initially empty remote location in The End. Press T, enter the command including the leading slash, and press Enter.
steps.success_cue: The game confirms Spectator mode, and the player can fly through blocks.

steps.action: Teleport the player into The End at the remote construction location. Press T, enter the command including the leading slash, and press Enter.
steps.success_cue: The player is in The End near X=1000.5, Y=96, Z=1000.5 and is safely hovering in Spectator mode.

steps.action: Wait before constructing anything at the remote location.
steps.success_cue: The surrounding End chunk has rendered, commands respond normally, and the player is no longer waiting on dimension or terrain loading.

steps.action: Create a 13-by-13 stone construction platform in the target End chunk. Press T, enter the command including the leading slash, and press Enter.
steps.success_cue: A stone platform covering X=994 through 1006 and Z=994 through 1006 is visible at Y=79.

steps.action: Create the glass shell for a vertical 1-by-1 stasis-chamber shaft. Press T, enter the command including the leading slash, and press Enter.
steps.success_cue: A solid 3-by-3 glass column extends from Y=80 through Y=88, centered on X=1000, Z=1000.

steps.action: Replace the center-bottom glass block with soul sand. Press T, enter the command including the leading slash, and press Enter.
steps.success_cue: Soul sand occupies X=1000, Y=80, Z=1000 and remains surrounded horizontally by glass.

steps.action: Replace the center of the glass shaft above the soul sand with water source blocks. Press T, enter the command including the leading slash, and press Enter.
steps.success_cue: The center shaft contains water from Y=81 through Y=88, with soul sand directly below it and an open top above Y=88.

steps.action: Allow the soul-sand bubble column to update.
steps.success_cue: Upward-moving bubble particles are visible throughout the water column, confirming that all eight water blocks form an upward bubble column.

steps.action: Place a repeating command block in the same chunk as the stasis chamber. Press T, enter the command including the leading slash, and press Enter.
steps.success_cue: A repeating command block is present at X=1004, Y=80, Z=1000. Both it and the chamber at X=1000, Z=1000 are inside the chunk bounded by X=992 through 1007 and Z=992 through 1007.

steps.action: Verify that The End has no administratively force-loaded chunks. Press T, enter the command including the leading slash, and press Enter.
steps.success_cue: The command reports that no chunks are marked for force loading in The End. Do not continue if any force-loaded End chunk is reported.

steps.action: Return to Creative mode. Press T, enter the command including the leading slash, and press Enter.
steps.success_cue: The game confirms Creative mode.

steps.action: Move beside the repeating command block. Press T, enter the command including the leading slash, and press Enter.
steps.success_cue: The player is standing on the End platform within interaction range of the command block at X=1004, Y=80, Z=1000.

steps.action: Aim the crosshair at the repeating command block and right-click it. In the command field, enter the exact command without a leading slash. Set the block type to Repeat, condition to Unconditional, and redstone mode to Always Active, then click Done.
steps.success_cue: The command-block interface closes and repeated chat messages containing MC-289348_HEARTBEAT begin appearing.

steps.action: Allow the command block to run briefly while the player is still in The End.
steps.success_cue: At least two successive MC-289348_HEARTBEAT messages have appeared, confirming that the repeating command block is configured and ticking before the pearl is thrown.

steps.action: Place one ender pearl directly into the first hotbar slot. Press T, enter the command including the leading slash, and press Enter.
steps.success_cue: An ender pearl is visible in the leftmost hotbar slot.

steps.action: Select the first hotbar slot using the default number key.
steps.success_cue: The ender pearl is shown in the player's hand, and the first hotbar slot is highlighted.

steps.action: Enable Creative flight by double-tapping the jump control before moving above the chamber.
steps.success_cue: The player is hovering in Creative flight and will not fall when teleported above the chamber.

steps.action: Move directly above the water column and face straight down. Press T, enter the command including the leading slash, and press Enter. The final pitch value of 90 points the view downward.
steps.success_cue: The player is hovering directly over the open top of the water column with the crosshair aimed straight down into it.

steps.action: With the ender pearl still selected, right-click exactly once to throw it downward into the water column.
steps.success_cue: One ender pearl projectile enters the water column. No second pearl has been thrown.

steps.action: Wait for the thrown pearl to stabilize in the soul-sand bubble column. Do not continue if the player is teleported or if the pearl escapes the chamber.
steps.success_cue: The thrown pearl remains visibly suspended or bobbing in the upper part of the bubble column, and the player has not been teleported by a pearl collision.

steps.action: Leave The End by teleporting back to the prepared Overworld platform. Press T, enter the command including the leading slash, and press Enter.
steps.success_cue: The player is standing on the stone platform at approximately X=0.5, Y=300, Z=0.5 in the Overworld; no player remains in The End.

steps.action: Wait for the Overworld to finish loading, then use the continuing command-block messages as a setup control before disconnecting.
steps.success_cue: Overworld terrain has rendered, movement responds normally, and at least two successive MC-289348_HEARTBEAT messages have appeared after the player left The End.

steps.action: Disconnect the test client without stopping the dedicated server.
steps.success_cue: The client has returned to the Multiplayer menu while the dedicated server process remains running.

steps.action: In the dedicated server console, verify that no players remain connected. Enter the command without a leading slash.
steps.success_cue: The server console reports zero connected players.

steps.action: Leave the dedicated server running with zero connected players for 20 real-time seconds. Do not pause, freeze, stop, or restart it during this interval.
steps.success_cue: At least 20 seconds have elapsed while the server continued ticking and no player was connected; this exceeds the 300-gametick interval described in the report comments at normal 20 TPS.

steps.action: Reconnect the same test account to the still-running server.
steps.exact_input: Multiplayer -> select the same server -> Join Server
steps.success_cue: The server accepts the connection and begins loading the test account at its saved Overworld location.

steps.action: Wait only until login and Overworld loading are complete. Do not enter The End, teleport toward the target coordinates, add a force-load ticket, or otherwise manually load the target End chunk.
steps.success_cue: The test account is fully connected in the Overworld, surrounding terrain is rendered, and movement responds normally; the target End chunk has not been manually loaded since reconnecting.

stor.handoff_condition: The same test account has just reconnected and finished loading in the Overworld after the dedicated server ticked for at least 20 seconds with no connected players. The suspended pearl and repeating command block remain at the remote End target coordinates, and no player or administrative force-load has manually reloaded that End chunk. Hand control to the observation subsystem now, before entering The End or approaching the target chunk.
uncertainties: The report does not provide the requested downloadable setup, a world seed, chamber dimensions, or construction coordinates. The remote platform, eight-block bubble column, and exact coordinates in this plan are deterministic practical choices that preserve the reported conditions.

The original steps do not explicitly require a dedicated server. A dedicated server is selected because it can continue processing the stated 300-gametick empty-dimension interval while the only client is disconnected; stopping an integrated single-player server would not provide the same controlled interval.

The report does not specify an exact disconnect duration. The 20-second wait is derived from the comment identifying 300 gameticks, equivalent to 15 seconds at normal 20 TPS, with a five-second execution margin.

The repeating command block executes the say command every game tick and can produce rapid chat and console output. Keep the pre-trigger portion brief and do not repeat the reproduction unnecessarily.
The stasis chamber must retain the pearl without causing a collision. If the pearl teleports the player or escapes, the chamber state was not established and the disconnect sequence must not be used.

source_meta._title: Mounted players/mobs trigger sculk sensors on world load

stor.environment: Minecraft: Java Edition 1.21.7 in a single-player world using the integrated server. Use Creative mode for deterministic access to the required blocks and items; a Superflat world is preferred but not required. Perform the final reload in 1.21.7, not the listed fix version 25w31a.
preconditions: The Minecraft Launcher has an installation configured for Java Edition 1.21.7.
Use a new or disposable single-player world so saving and reloading cannot affect an important world.
Use an open, level test area with no wool blocks between the sensors and the minecart, and keep unrelated entities away from the area.
The calibrated sculk sensor must continuously receive redstone signal strength 6 through its calibration input side.
The minecart and seated player must remain within range of both sensors throughout the save-and-reload sequence.
Use the default controls described below or the equivalent controls if key bindings have been changed.

steps.action: In the Minecraft Launcher, start the installation that explicitly shows Java Edition 1.21.7. Do not use 25w31a or a newer version for this reproduction.
steps.success_cue: The main menu displays Minecraft Java Edition 1.21.7.

steps.action: Open Singleplayer and create a new world. Set Game Mode to Creative. For a deterministic level building area, open the World settings and select the Superflat world type, then create the world.
steps.exact_input: Singleplayer -> Create New World -> Game Mode: Creative -> World: Superflat -> Create New World
steps.success_cue: The player is in a Creative-mode single-player world on a level surface.

steps.action: Wait without performing the test until terrain has rendered and movement responds normally. Move to an open area with enough room for two sensors, a three-block calibration circuit, and a nearby minecart.
steps.success_cue: The surrounding ground is loaded and there is a clear test area at least 10 blocks across.

steps.action: Press E to open the Creative inventory. Use the Search Items tab and place the following in the hotbar, which is the nine-slot row at the bottom of the screen: Sculk Sensor, Calibrated Sculk Sensor, Redstone Comparator, Jukebox, the music disc found by searching for “mall”, Rail, and Minecart. Close the inventory with E or Esc.
steps.exact_input: E; search for: sculk sensor, calibrated sculk sensor, comparator, jukebox, mall, rail, minecart
steps.success_cue: All seven required block/item types are accessible from the hotbar or Creative inventory.

steps.action: Select the regular Sculk Sensor in the hotbar and press the use control, default right-click, on the level ground to place it. Leave the block above it unobstructed.
steps.success_cue: One regular sculk sensor is placed with its tendrils visible.

steps.action: Select the Calibrated Sculk Sensor and place it on the same ground level, approximately two blocks from the regular sensor. Inspect its sides and leave the amethyst-covered calibration input side facing into open space; if necessary, break and replace it from another direction. A calibrated sensor listens only for the vibration frequency matching the signal supplied to this input side. ([minecraft.wiki](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Category%3ABlock_textures?utm_source=openai))
steps.exact_input: Select Calibrated Sculk Sensor; right-click ground
steps.success_cue: The regular and calibrated sensors are both present, and the calibrated sensor's amethyst input side is accessible.

steps.action: Select the Redstone Comparator. Stand behind the intended comparator position while facing the calibrated sensor's amethyst input side, then place the comparator directly adjacent to that side. Orient it so its front/output end points into the calibrated sensor and its two-torch rear/input end points away from the sensor.
steps.exact_input: Select Redstone Comparator; right-click the block adjacent to the calibrated sensor's amethyst side
steps.success_cue: The comparator directly touches the calibrated sensor's input side and points toward the sensor.

steps.action: Select the Jukebox and place it directly behind the comparator, against the comparator's rear/input end. The resulting straight layout must be: jukebox -> comparator -> calibrated sensor input side.
steps.exact_input: Select Jukebox; right-click the block directly behind the comparator
steps.success_cue: The jukebox is directly behind the comparator, with no gap or intervening block.

steps.action: Select the music disc named “C418 - mall” or found by searching “mall”, aim at the jukebox, and press the use control, default right-click, once to insert it. A comparator reading this disc supplies signal strength 6, providing the report's required calibration value. The comparator continues reading the stored disc even after its music finishes. ([zh.minecraft.wiki](https://zh.minecraft.wiki/w/%E7%BA%A2%E7%9F%B3%E6%AF%94%E8%BE%83%E5%99%A8?utm_source=openai))
steps.exact_input: Select Music Disc C418 - mall; right-click jukebox once
steps.success_cue: The disc is stored in the jukebox and the comparator remains directed from the jukebox into the calibrated sensor's input side.

steps.action: Select the Rail and place one rail on the level ground at a position no more than four horizontal blocks from each sensor. Keep the rail away from the comparator and jukebox so the minecart will not collide with the calibration circuit.
steps.exact_input: Select Rail; right-click ground within four blocks of both sensors
steps.success_cue: A single rail is visible close to both sensors.

steps.action: Select the Minecart and press the use control, default right-click, on the rail to place the minecart. Do not enter it yet.
steps.success_cue: An empty minecart is stationary on the rail and remains within four blocks of both sensors.

steps.action: Stop placing or using blocks and remain unmounted. Wait until both sensors have returned to their inactive appearance and no vibration particle is traveling toward either sensor. If their state is difficult to judge, remain still for at least five seconds.
steps.success_cue: The player is not riding anything, the minecart is empty, and both sensors are idle.

steps.action: Establish the report's unmounted reload state. Press Esc, click Save and Quit to Title, and wait until the title screen appears.
steps.exact_input: Esc -> Save and Quit to Title
steps.success_cue: The title screen is visible and the world has been saved while the player was unmounted.

steps.action: Open Singleplayer, select the same test world, and click Play Selected World. Do not select a different world or recreate the setup.
steps.exact_input: Singleplayer -> select the saved test world -> Play Selected World
steps.success_cue: The same world has loaded with the player standing near the empty minecart and sensor setup.

steps.action: Do not move or interact with the setup after loading. Wait until surrounding chunks have rendered, controls respond normally, and both sensors are idle. Confirm that the player is still outside the minecart.
steps.success_cue: The world is responsive, the player is unmounted, the minecart is empty, and both sensors are ready to receive a new vibration.

steps.action: Approach only as far as necessary to reach the minecart. Center the crosshair on the minecart and press the use control, default right-click, once to mount it. Do not press the sneak/dismount control, default Left Shift, afterward.
steps.exact_input: Right-click the minecart; do not press Left Shift
steps.success_cue: The viewpoint is seated in the minecart and the player remains within range of both sensors.

steps.action: Remain seated and do not move the minecart. Wait until both sensors have completely returned to their inactive appearance after the mounting action. If uncertain, wait at least five seconds while remaining mounted.
steps.success_cue: The player is still seated in the stationary minecart and both sensors are idle before the world is saved.

steps.action: While still seated in the minecart, press Esc and click Save and Quit to Title. Do not dismount before selecting Save and Quit.
steps.exact_input: Esc -> Save and Quit to Title
steps.success_cue: The title screen is visible, and the world was saved with the player seated in the minecart near both sensors.

steps.action: Click Singleplayer once and select the same saved test world, but do not press Play Selected World yet.
steps.exact_input: Singleplayer -> select the saved test world
steps.success_cue: The correct 1.21.7 test world is highlighted in the world list and is ready to load.

steps.action: Click Play Selected World once to reload the world containing the already-mounted player. Hand control to the observation subsystem as soon as loading begins; do not wait to perform another player action after terrain appears.
steps.success_cue: The loading screen for the saved test world has begun, with the saved player-minecart riding relationship still present in the world data.

stor.handoff_condition: The same Java Edition 1.21.7 world has just begun loading after being saved while the player was seated in the minecart within range of the regular and signal-6-calibrated sculk sensors. Begin observation during loading and continue through the first seconds after terrain appears, without moving, dismounting, or interacting with the setup.
uncertainties: The report does not specify a game mode, world seed, coordinates, or world type. Creative mode and a Superflat world are selected only to make item acquisition and placement deterministic.
The report permits several mountable entities. This plan uses a stationary minecart as the simplest deterministic player-mount variant supported by the report.

The report also includes a separate non-player entity variant using /ride. This plan selects the player variant because the instructions direct selection of the simplest deterministic reproduction when multiple variants are available.

The jukebox, comparator, and “mall” music disc circuit is an externally verified practical method of supplying the required signal strength 6; the report specifies the signal strength but not how it must be generated.

No exact sensor-to-mount distance is supplied. The plan uses no more than four horizontal blocks from the minecart to each sensor, which conservatively satisfies the report's requirement that the mount remain within both sensors' radii.

source_meta.issue links: Relates:outward:MC-302405:Repeating/chain command blocks with any form of a '/tp <player>' command doesn't constantly teleport the player to one spot
source_meta._title: Chunks don't load while the player is being teleported

stor.environment: Minecraft Java Edition 1.21.9 Release Candidate 1; a new single-player world using the integrated server; Creative mode with commands/cheats enabled; Superflat world selected as a deterministic unobstructed test area; repeating command block placed beside the world's initial spawn point so it remains in a loaded spawn chunk; Render Distance set to 12 chunks.
preconditions: Use Minecraft Java Edition, not Bedrock Edition.
Launch exactly 1.21.9 Release Candidate 1, the first version listed as affected. Do not use the listed fix version, 1.21.10 Release Candidate 1.
Use a disposable single-player world with commands available. Creative mode is selected to simplify command-block acquisition and prevent terrain or survival hazards from interrupting the test.
Use a Superflat world as a practical deterministic choice because the report supplies no seed, coordinates, terrain type, or world file.
Perform the setup close to the position where the player initially spawns. Do not travel away before placing the command block.
Ensure no other player is present. This makes the report's @p[tag=p] selector deterministically target the local player after the p tag is added.
Do not give the player the p tag until the repeating command block has been completely configured.
The command block must be configured as Repeat, Unconditional, and Always Active. Because the selector initially finds no player with the p tag, it can safely remain active during setup.
Keep the report-supplied stop command `/tag @s remove p` available. Do not execute it before the active-teleport observation handoff.
The controls named below assume the default Java Edition bindings. If controls were rebound, use the binding for the stated action.

steps.action: In the Minecraft Launcher, create or select an installation for the exact affected version 1.21.9 Release Candidate 1, start it, and wait for the Java Edition title screen.
steps.success_cue: The title screen identifies the running game as Minecraft Java Edition 1.21.9 Release Candidate 1.

steps.action: Open Singleplayer and create a new disposable world. Set Game Mode to Creative, make sure commands are permitted, and select the Superflat world type from the world settings before creating the world.
steps.exact_input: Singleplayer -> Create New World -> Game Mode: Creative; World Type: Superflat; commands/cheats enabled
steps.success_cue: A new Superflat Creative world begins loading.

steps.action: Wait without traveling away from the initial spawn area until terrain has rendered and normal movement and UI input respond without world-loading delay.
steps.success_cue: The player is standing on fully rendered flat terrain near the world's initial spawn position, and controls respond normally.

steps.action: Set Render Distance to 12 chunks to establish a known initial loading radius. Pause the game, open Options, open Video Settings, set Render Distance to 12 chunks, apply the setting, and return to the world.
steps.exact_input: Esc -> Options -> Video Settings -> Render Distance: 12 chunks -> Done
steps.success_cue: The player is back in the world with Render Distance set to 12 chunks and surrounding terrain has finished rendering.

steps.action: Open chat, enter the command that gives the executing player one command block, and submit it. Include the leading slash because this command is being run through in-game chat.
steps.success_cue: The give command succeeds and a Command Block appears in the inventory, normally in an available hotbar slot.

steps.action: Select the hotbar slot containing the Command Block. The hotbar is the row of nine item slots at the bottom of the screen; press the corresponding number key or scroll the mouse wheel until the Command Block is outlined as the active item.
steps.exact_input: Number key 1-9 or mouse wheel, matching the Command Block's hotbar slot
steps.success_cue: A Command Block is visible in the player's hand and its hotbar slot is highlighted.

steps.action: While still beside the world's initial spawn position, aim at the top of a nearby ground block and use the selected Command Block to place it.
steps.success_cue: A command block is placed on the ground within a few blocks of the initial spawn position.

steps.action: Aim at the placed command block and use it to open the command-block configuration screen.
steps.success_cue: The command-block configuration screen is open and contains a command input field plus block-mode controls.

steps.action: Enter the report's command exactly into the command-block command field. Do not add a leading slash in the command block.
steps.success_cue: The command field contains exactly `execute as @p[tag=p] at @s run tp @s ~ ~ ~1`, including the selector, spaces, tildes, and final 1.

steps.action: Change the command block's block type from its default impulse mode to repeating mode by clicking the block-type control until it displays Repeat.
steps.success_cue: The block-type control displays Repeat.

steps.action: Ensure the command block's condition setting displays Unconditional. If it displays Conditional, click it once to change it.
steps.success_cue: The condition control displays Unconditional.

steps.action: Change the activation setting to Always Active so that the repeating command executes continuously without a lever or other redstone source.
steps.success_cue: The activation control displays Always Active.

steps.action: Save the command-block configuration by selecting Done.
steps.success_cue: The configuration screen closes, the command block has the purple repeating-command-block appearance, and the player is not yet being teleported because no player currently has the p tag.

steps.action: Stand on the flat surface beside the command block. Open the debug overlay and orient the camera toward positive Z so the direction of travel is visible. With default controls, press F3 and turn until the Facing line says south, toward positive Z. Note the current Z coordinate shown in the overlay.
steps.success_cue: The F3 overlay is visible, the Facing line indicates south/toward positive Z, and the player's starting Z coordinate can be read.

steps.action: Open in-game chat, enter the report-supplied command that gives the executing player the p tag, and submit it. Include the leading slash. This activates the repeating command block's selector and is the reproduction trigger.
steps.success_cue: The tag command succeeds and the F3 Z coordinate immediately begins increasing repeatedly without the player pressing a movement key.

steps.action: Release all movement controls and allow the command block to continue teleporting the tagged player. Do not pause, remove the tag, or manually move. Wait until the F3 Z coordinate has increased by at least 224 blocks from the coordinate noted before triggering; at 12-chunk Render Distance, this carries the player beyond the initially rendered radius and requires additional chunks along positive Z.
steps.exact_input: Wait with no movement input until current Z >= starting Z + 224
steps.success_cue: The player still has the p tag, is still being moved repeatedly in positive Z by the command block, and has traveled at least 224 blocks from the trigger position.

stor.handoff_condition: The player is still tagged p and the spawn-area repeating command block is continuously executing `execute as @p[tag=p] at @s run tp @s ~ ~ ~1`, moving the player one block in positive Z per execution. The player has traveled at least 224 blocks beyond the trigger position with no manual movement. Begin active-teleport chunk-loading observation now, before executing the report-supplied stop command `/tag @s remove p`.
uncertainties: The report does not specify a world seed, world type, coordinates, game mode, render distance, or whether the test was performed in single-player or on a dedicated server. This plan uses a new single-player Creative Superflat world and Render Distance 12 as deterministic practical choices.

The report does not state where the repeating command block was placed. This plan places it beside the initial world spawn so that continuous teleportation does not unload the command block and prematurely stop command execution.

The report calls for a repeating command block but does not explicitly name its condition or redstone settings. Unconditional and Always Active are used so the supplied command executes continuously without adding an unrelated redstone clock.

The report's `/tag @s remove p` command is a post-observation stop/control action. It is deliberately not executed before handoff because doing so would end the active teleport condition that triggers the reported behavior. After the active state has been captured, that exact command can be entered in chat to stop teleportation.
The comment describing the same behavior while riding a teleported entity is an additional variant, not part of the primary reproduction path, and is therefore not included.
